warnings: *** THIS IS THE AUTHORITATIVE DOOR SCHEDULE THAT A-04, A-05, A-06, A-07 AND A-08 WERE DEFERRED TO. *** Every one of those plan and elevation files recorded rooms, levels and notes but deliberately did NOT transcribe the circled ป marks, because the glyphs are about ten pixels tall on those sheets and misreading a ป3 as a ป8 would invent a mark. The set has exactly eight door types, ป1 to ป8, drawn here at 1:50 with full specifications. Marking which opening on which plan is which type still needs the full-size sheets; this file establishes the vocabulary, not the positions.

EACH DOOR CARRIES TWO WIDTHS AND THEY MEAN DIFFERENT THINGS. The upper figure is the วงกบ (frame) opening and the lower is the บาน (leaf), e.g. ป2 at 0.90 / 0.80. width_mm records the frame opening - the dimension a builder sets out - and leaf_width_mm the leaf. ป1 is the exception: at 2.40 m it prints only the overall and its internal division 0.55 + 0.60 + 0.60 + 0.55, which closes exactly, and that split is kept in the note.

ป1 IS THE ONLY ALUMINIUM DOOR IN THE HOUSE - a double leaf with fixed glass side panels, aluminium frame and leaf, 5 mm clear glass. Every other door is a timber ไม้เต็ง frame with a ไม้สัก, ไม้อัดยาง or ไฟเบอร์ leaf. That matches the elevations, where the front entrance reads as a wide glazed unit and everything else as a solid panel.
ป5 IS SPECIFIED AS ไฟเบอร์สำเร็จรูป WITH NO PAINT NOTE, unlike every other timber door which carries a ทาสีน้ำมัน instruction. Recorded as printed; the omission is the sheet's, not this extraction's.

THE WINDOW IRONMONGERY LIST IS PRINTED ON THIS SHEET but the windows themselves are on A-15. Both hardware lists are recorded here because that is where they are printed; the window list names four leaf types (บานเลื่อน, เกร็ดกระจก, บานกระทุ้ง, บานมุ้งลวด) all with aluminium frames, which is the first indication that the windows are aluminium rather than timber.

The doors are recorded with element_type door and the printed Thai ป marks as element_id, per §0.1's rule that door/window entries live in elements[] and §0.3's rule that the mark is recorded exactly as printed - not normalised to a D-series.
